summary: Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge in 2016 under Eivind Kahrs, and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design in 2019.

Alessandro Graheli is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. In 2022, he was attested as a university assistant at the University of Vienna and a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Alex McKay is a historian and Tibetologist. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford and SOAS, supervised by Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, and held posts at Harvard University, Wolfson College, Oxford, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Educated at UCLA and UC Berkeley under Ferdinand Lessing and Murray Barnson Emeneau, he held posts at UC Berkeley, the University of Michigan, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Columbia University.

Alexander Berzin is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He co-founded the translation bureau at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and serves on advisory boards in Germany and Thailand.

Alexander C. Soper was a scholar of archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hamilton College and Princeton University before holding long-term faculty appointments at Bryn Mawr College and New York University.

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Bethlen Gábor College and the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn. He later served as librarian for The Asiatic Society.

Alexander Cunningham was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Christ's Hospital and Addiscombe Military Seminary, studying under James Prinsep. He founded and led the Archaeological Survey of India, serving as its first director and later director-general.
Alexander Duff was a scholar of religious studies and history who studied at the University of St Andrews and the University of Aberdeen.
Alexander Freiman studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy from approximately 1903 to 1907 and under Christian Bartholomae between 1906 and 1907.

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan in 2006 under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and holds a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander Hamilton was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Hindu Literature at the East India Company College starting in 1806.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has pursued PhD studies at the University of Toronto and held a research fellowship at Taisho University.

Alexander Johnston was an Indologist and historian who studied law at the University of Göttingen and Lincoln's Inn. He founded the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland and served as chief justice on the Executive Council of Ceylon.

Alexander Kabanoff was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies. In 2000, he was attested as Senior Researcher at Saint Petersburg State University and head of the Japanese section at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Alexander Kasimovich Kazembek was a linguist and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held academic posts at Kazan Imperial University from 1826 to 1849 and at Imperial St. Petersburg University from 1849 to 1870.

Alexander Lubotsky is a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Moscow State University and Leiden University under Robert S. P. Beekes, later becoming full professor of Comparative Indo-European Linguistics at Leiden in 1999.
Alexander Murray was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh from 1794 to 1802 and held a post there from 1812 to 1813.

Alexander O. Hsu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago Divinity School under Paul Copp and Christian K. Wedemeyer, and held a teaching post at North Dakota State University.
